business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business overview.
business_model.claim: Micron sells semiconductor memory and storage products—DRAM, NAND, and NOR—across data center, mobile, client, automotive, industrial, and consumer end markets.
quotes: We are a global leader in semiconductor memory and storage, powering AI and compute-intensive applications from cloud to edge.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (Item 1) and confirmed by F2 income statement.
business_model.claim: In fiscal 2026, DRAM generated $100.68 billion in revenue and NAND generated $31.79 billion, together accounting for the vast majority of total revenue of $133,188 million (table in millions).
quotes: Total reported DRAM revenue was $100.68 billion in 2026, $28.58 billion in 2025, and $17.60 billion in 2024.
Total reported NAND revenue was $31.79 billion in 2026, $8.50 billion in 2025, and $7.23 billion in 2024.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A revenue-by-business-unit table and Item 1 descriptions.
business_model.claim: Micron reports revenue in four business units: Cloud Memory (CMBU, $43,085 million), Core Data Center (CDBU, $37,592 million), Mobile and Client (MCBU, $36,601 million), and Automotive and Embedded (AEBU, $15,886 million) for fiscal 2026 (table in millions).

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A Results of Operations section.
business_model.claim: Revenue growth in fiscal 2026 was driven primarily by average selling price increases (approximately 180% for DRAM and 200% for NAND) plus a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments for both product lines.
quotes: Sales of DRAM products increased 252% primarily due to an approximate 180% increase in average selling prices and a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments.
Sales of NAND products increased 274% primarily due to an approximate 200% increase in average selling prices and a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments.

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 Risk Factors and P3 MD&A; figures confirmed in F2 income statement.
business_model.claim: Gross margin is determined by average selling prices and the ability to reduce per-gigabit manufacturing costs through process and product design improvements; consolidated gross margin percentage was 81% in fiscal 2026 versus 40% in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Our gross margins are dependent upon our average selling prices, as well as our ability to continue decreasing per gigabit manufacturing costs, which is primarily achieved through improvements in our manufacturing processes and product designs.
Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 81% for 2026 from 40% for 2025 as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A Liquidity and Capital Resources section; deposit figure confirmed in F3 cash flow statement (Proceeds from customer contract liability deposits: $12,747 million).
business_model.claim: Micron entered strategic customer agreements in Q3 and Q4 of fiscal 2026 structured as take-or-pay contracts with multi-year volume commitments, and received $12.75 billion in customer deposits in 2026.
quotes: Strategic customer agreements are structured as take-or-pay agreements, with binding commitments for specific volumes over the multi-year contract terms.
In connection with these strategic customer agreements, we received cash deposits of $12.75 billion in 2026.

business_model.basis: Stated in F2 income statement and P3 MD&A operating expense discussion.
business_model.claim: Operating expenses in fiscal 2026 consisted of R&D of $5,650 million, SG&A of $1,947 million, and other operating expense of $567 million (table in millions), producing operating income of $99,340 million.
quotes: Research and development | 5,650 | 4%
Selling, general, and administrative | 1,947 | 1%
Operating income | 99,340 | 75%

business_model.basis: Stated in P3 MD&A Liquidity and Capital Resources; capex figure confirmed in F3.
business_model.claim: Micron funds its capital-intensive manufacturing expansion through operating cash flow, CHIPS Act grants of up to $6.4 billion, a 35% investment tax credit, customer contract deposits, and a $2.00 billion revolving credit facility.
quotes: The grants under the funding agreements represent total CHIPS Act grants of up to $6.4 billion in connection with our U.S. manufacturing expansion and modernization projects.
As of September 3, 2026, $2.00 billion was available to draw under our Revolving Credit Facility.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A) and corroborated by F2 income statement figures.
competitive_position.claim: Micron's fiscal 2026 revenue of $133,188 (table in millions) represented a 256% increase over fiscal 2025, driven by both DRAM and NAND product sales.
quotes: Total revenue for 2026 increased 256% as compared to 2025 primarily due to increases in sales of both DRAM and NAND products.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P3; gross margin of $107,504 (table in millions) on revenue of $133,188 (table in millions) is shown in F2.
competitive_position.claim: Micron's consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 81% in fiscal 2026 from 40% in fiscal 2025, reflecting pricing power and cost reductions.
quotes: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 81% for 2026 from 40% for 2025 as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A Industry Conditions) and P1 (Business overview). Management's Q1-27 guidance of approximately 85.95% GAAP gross margin (P4) implies the condition persists.
competitive_position.claim: AI-driven memory and storage demand growth is outpacing industry supply, creating a structural tailwind for Micron's pricing and profitability.
quotes: AI-driven memory and storage demand growth is outpacing industry supply.
The AI-driven growth in the data center has accelerated demand for memory and storage at a rate greater than our ability and the industry's ability to increase supply.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P1 (Business, CMBU section) and P3 (MD&A). CMBU revenue of $43.09 billion in 2026 (P1) reflects the data-center/HBM demand.
competitive_position.claim: Micron holds a leading position in High-Bandwidth Memory, with HBM3E 12-high as the majority of 2026 HBM shipments, HBM4 36GB 12-high in volume production, and HBM4E development expected to ramp in calendar 2027.
quotes: In 2026, HBM3E 12-high represented the majority of our HBM shipments.

we began volume production of our HBM4 36GB 12-high with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our 1β (1-beta) process node, and we delivered samples of HBM4 48GB 16-high to multiple key customers to power next-generation AI platforms.
Development of HBM4E, our next-generation HBM product leveraging our 1γ DRAM technology node, is well underway, and we expect to ramp volume in calendar 2027.

competitive_position.claim: Micron was first to ship its 1γ DRAM production node, the industry's first DRAM node incorporating EUV lithography, and the majority of its DRAM bit production in Q4 2026 was on this leading-edge node.
quotes: In 2025, we began shipping the industry's first 1γ (1-gamma) production node, which is our first DRAM node incorporating EUV lithography and offers further improvements in power efficiency, performance, and bit density compared to our prior DRAM node products.
The majority of our DRAM bit production in the fourth quarter of 2026 was on our leading-edge 1γ node.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A, Liquidity and Capital Resources). The $12,747 (table in millions) proceeds from customer contract liability deposits appear in F3 cash flow statement.
competitive_position.claim: Micron entered into strategic customer agreements structured as take-or-pay contracts with binding multi-year volume commitments, receiving $12.75 billion in customer deposits in 2026, which management states will yield gross margins meaningfully above any prior peak cycle quarter even at floor pricing.
quotes: Strategic customer agreements are structured as take-or-pay agreements, with binding commitments for specific volumes over the multi-year contract terms.
We expect gross margins from our strategic customer agreements with price bands, even at floor pricing levels, to yield gross margins meaningfully above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle.
In connection with these strategic customer agreements, we received cash deposits of $12.75 billion in 2026.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors, competition section).
competitive_position.claim: Micron faces intense competition from Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk, ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), some of which are state-backed.
quotes: We face intense competition in the semiconductor memory and storage markets from a number of companies, including Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.; SK hynix Inc.; Kioxia Holdings Corporation; Sandisk Corporation; ChangXin Memory Technologies, Inc. ("CXMT"); and Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., Ltd. ("YMTC").

we face the threat of increasing competition and DRAM and NAND oversupply due to significant investment in the semiconductor industry, including by the Chinese government and various state-owned or affiliated entities, such as CXMT and YMTC.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors, international operations).
competitive_position.claim: China's CAC determined in May 2023 that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products, restricting revenue from mainland China and Hong Kong customers.
quotes: Following the May 2023 decision of its cybersecurity review of our products sold in China, the CAC determined that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products, impacting our revenue with companies headquartered in mainland China and Hong Kong, including direct sales, as well as indirect sales through distributors.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors, ASP volatility).
competitive_position.claim: Micron's average selling prices have historically ranged from an increase of approximately 200% to a decrease of approximately 50% annually over the past five fiscal years, creating cyclical revenue and margin volatility risk.
quotes: Over the past five fiscal years, annual percentage changes in DRAM and NAND average selling prices have ranged from an increase of approximately 200% to a decrease of approximately 50%.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors, international operations and Taiwan-specific risk).
competitive_position.claim: Approximately 70% of Micron's 2026 revenue was from products shipped to customer locations outside the United States, and a majority of its DRAM production output in 2026 was from fabrication facilities in Taiwan, creating geopolitical concentration risk.
quotes: approximately 70% of our revenue in 2026 was from products shipped to customer locations outside the United States.
A majority of our DRAM production output in 2026 was from our fabrication facilities in Taiwan, and any loss of output could have a material adverse effect on us.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A, Liquidity and Capital Resources) and P1 (Business).
competitive_position.claim: Micron has committed to up to $6.4 billion in CHIPS Act grants for U.S. manufacturing expansion, with fabs in Boise, Idaho (first wafer output mid-calendar 2027; second fab by late 2028), Clay, New York (initial output calendar 2030), and Manassas, Virginia, plus a planned $10 billion investment in Micron Research Labs in Boise.
quotes: The grants under the funding agreements represent total CHIPS Act grants of up to $6.4 billion in connection with our U.S. manufacturing expansion and modernization projects.

we announced the establishment of Micron Research Labs, a long-horizon research institution headquartered in Boise, Idaho, supported by a planned investment of approximately $10 billion over the next decade to advance memory, compute and semiconductor manufacturing technologies.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A Industry Conditions) and P1 (Business description); the revenue figures are from the consolidated results table in P3.
growth_thesis.claim: AI-driven data center demand for HBM, DDR5, and LPDDR5 is the primary growth engine, with CMBU revenue of $43,085 (table in millions) in fiscal 2026 versus $3,792 (table in millions) in fiscal 2024, and for this to continue, AI infrastructure capital expenditure by hyperscale and NeoCloud customers must sustain or accelerate, and HBM/DDR5 demand must outpace new industry supply.
quotes: AI-driven memory and storage demand growth is outpacing industry supply.

Cloud servers supporting AI and data-centric workloads require significantly increasing quantities of DRAM, including HBM, and NAND as the task of turning data into insight becomes increasingly memory-centric.
In 2026, HBM3E 12-high represented the majority of our HBM shipments.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A Strategic Customer Agreements section); the $12.75 billion deposit figure and $7 billion letters of credit are explicitly stated in P3.
growth_thesis.claim: Strategic Customer Agreements (take-or-pay contracts) entered in Q3 and Q4 of 2026 provide contracted volume and pricing visibility, and for this driver to continue, customers must meet minimum purchase commitments over multi-year terms and the pricing bands must remain at levels that yield gross margins 'meaningfully above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle.'
quotes: Strategic customer agreements are structured as take-or-pay agreements, with binding commitments for specific volumes over the multi-year contract terms.
We expect gross margins from our strategic customer agreements with price bands, even at floor pricing levels, to yield gross margins meaningfully above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle.
In connection with these strategic customer agreements, we received cash deposits of $12.75 billion in 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A Results of Operations, Total Revenue section); the historical range is stated in P2 (Risk Factors, ASP volatility).
growth_thesis.claim: Average selling price increases were the dominant factor in fiscal 2026 revenue growth—DRAM ASPs rose approximately 180% and NAND ASPs approximately 200%—and for this to continue, industry supply growth must remain below demand growth and competitors must not flood the market with excess capacity.
quotes: Sales of DRAM products increased 252% primarily due to an approximate 180% increase in average selling prices and a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments.
Sales of NAND products increased 274% primarily due to an approximate 200% increase in average selling prices and a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments.

In recent periods, industry demand has outpaced supply, driving average selling prices higher, but as we and others increase supply, average selling prices may decline, particularly if demand growth slows or declines.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A Consolidated Gross Margin) and P4 (FQ4-26 quarterly table showing 86.8%); the FQ1-27 guidance of 85.95% is from P4.
growth_thesis.claim: Gross margin expanded to 81% in fiscal 2026 from 40% in fiscal 2025 and reached 86.8% in FQ4-26, and for this trajectory to continue, ASPs must hold or grow, manufacturing cost reductions from process transitions must be sustained, and product mix must remain weighted toward high-margin HBM and data center products.
quotes: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 81% for 2026 from 40% for 2025 as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products.
Margins improved primarily due to increases in average selling prices and also benefited from favorable mix and manufacturing cost reductions due to continued strong execution.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A Liquidity and Capital Resources); the $6.4 billion CHIPS Act total and 35% ITC are explicitly stated in P3.
growth_thesis.claim: New fab construction in Idaho, New York, Singapore, Taiwan, and Japan—supported by up to $6.4 billion in CHIPS Act grants and a 35% investment tax credit—will add DRAM and NAND wafer capacity to support projected demand, and for this to continue, construction must complete on schedule, specialized equipment and labor must be available, and government funding must be disbursed without clawback.
quotes: we estimate capital expenditures for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $11.5 billion in the first quarter of 2027, approximately $25 billion in the first six months of 2027, and higher in the second half of 2027.
Construction of the fab began in October 2023, with first DRAM wafer output projected in mid-calendar 2027.
The grants under the funding agreements represent total CHIPS Act grants of up to $6.4 billion in connection with our U.S. manufacturing expansion and modernization projects.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (Business, Product Technologies); the competitive landscape and yield risks are stated in P2 (Risk Factors).
growth_thesis.claim: Technology node transitions—1γ DRAM (first EUV node, ramping to highest-volume node), HBM4 volume production, and G9 NAND—maintain Micron's competitive edge, and for this to continue, acceptable yields and quality must be achieved at scale, customers must complete qualification, and competitors (Samsung, SK hynix, CXMT, YMTC) must not leapfrog on key metrics.
quotes: In 2025, we began shipping the industry's first 1γ (1-gamma) production node, which is our first DRAM node incorporating EUV lithography and offers further improvements in power efficiency, performance, and bit density compared to our prior DRAM node products.

In 2026, we began volume production of our HBM4 36GB 12-high with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our 1β (1-beta) process node, and we delivered samples of HBM4 48GB 16-high to multiple key customers to power next-generation AI platforms.
The majority of our DRAM bit production in the fourth quarter of 2026 was on our leading-edge 1γ node.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in F1 (balance sheet), F3 (cash flow statement), P3 (MD&A Liquidity), and P4 (earnings release). The $73.45 billion and $35.16 billion figures are explicitly stated in P3.
growth_thesis.claim: Micron's balance sheet strengthened dramatically in fiscal 2026, with total equity of $138,378 (table in millions) and cash plus marketable investments of $73.45 billion, providing the financial capacity to fund the $25 billion+ H1-2027 capex program and the expanded $35.16 billion share repurchase authorization, and for this to continue, operating cash flow must remain elevated and debt levels must not spike.
quotes: Cash and marketable investments totaled $73.45 billion as of September 3, 2026, and $11.94 billion as of August 28, 2025.
on October 8, 2026 our Board of Directors authorized an increase in the maximum amount of discretionary repurchases of our outstanding common stock to be made from December 9, 2026 to $35.16 billion.

risks.basis: stated in P2 risk factors (new product development and HBM-specific risk)
risks.claim: If HBM demand weakens, the industry-wide shift of capacity from HBM back to conventional DRAM could cause a significant oversupply of conventional DRAM and downward pricing pressure.
quotes: HBM requires a higher number of wafers and more cleanroom space to produce the same number of bits as conventional DRAM in the same technology node. An oversupplied DRAM market may lead to downward pressure on pricing, which could adversely impact our financial results.
